title: Basic SIR Model
text: use data simulated basic SIR model 500 households. assume individuals start susceptible. per day intra-household infection probability 5% daily extra-household infection probability 1%.

title: Basic SIR Model
text: addition data, user needs specify underlying model structure, involves two components: infection process model specifies underlying compartmental model structure. observation process model specifies probability observing positive outcome given individual compartment infection process model.

title: Basic SIR Model
text: infection process model built series user-defined transitions. two types transitions: transmit() defines transition occurs result infection (e.g. S>) progress() defines non-infection transition occurs constant rate (e.g. ->R). functions, user specifies destination (e.g = S) source (e.g = ) compartment. Additionally progress() transitions, user must enter parameter transition rate. name parameter discretion user (e.g. gamma recovery rate) can set specific numeric value NA model fit parameter.
code: # Basic SIR, fit recovery rate inf_process <- make_infection_model(transmit(from = "S", to = "I"),                                     progress(from = "I", to = "R", gamma = NA))

title: Basic SIR Model
text: observation model composed series named vectors. vector corresponds observation type. entry vector named corresponding compartment infection process model. value probability observing positive observation given individual compartment. example two observation types, one likely positive person actively infectious (e.g. PCR test results) likely positive person recovered immune infection (e.g. IgG antibody). Now ready run model! Now let’s look model results using posterior package.
code: obs_process <- make_observation_model(   pcr = c("S" = 0.05, "I" = 0.95, "R" = 0.05),   igg = c("S" = 0.01, "I" = 0.01, "R" = 0.8) ) # Note this is very computationally intensive so the block is not evaluated # when knitting  ## Inputs # 1. Infection process model # 2. Observation process model # 3. Raw data # 4. Covariates (optional) # 5. Starting state probabilities  sir_res <- run_model(   inf_model = inf_process,   obs_model = obs_process,   data = sir,   init_probs = c(1 - 2 * 1e-10, 1e-10, 1e-10),   iter = 1000,   cores = 4 ) # The output from the model in the previous code chunk is available in the # sir_res package data object  # Get summary statistics, note that parameters are returned on the logit scale # so we also transform back to arithmetic scale draws_sum <- summarise_draws(sir_res, "mean", "median", ~ quantile2(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) |>   mutate(var_type = c(rep("Infection probability", 2), "Recovery rate")) %>%   mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ plogis(.x)))  # "True" values from underlying simulation draws_sum$true_value <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.2)   draws_sum ## # A tibble: 3 × 7 ##   variable    mean  median    q2.5  q97.5 var_type              true_value ##   <chr>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>                      <dbl> ## 1 eh_prob  0.00985 0.00986 0.00918 0.0105 Infection probability       0.01 ## 2 ih_prob  0.0544  0.0545  0.0491  0.0604 Infection probability       0.05 ## 3 gamma    0.202   0.202   0.192   0.213  Recovery rate               0.2

title: Basic SIR Model
text: can add covariates intra- extra-household infection risk including optional ih_cov eh_cov arguments, respectively, run_model(). Let’s take look results .
code: # Simulated data from a basic SIR model for 500 households head(sir_cov$observations)  # Run model with x1 and x2 as covariates sir_cov_res <- run_model(   inf_model = inf_process,   obs_model = obs_process,   data = sir_cov$observations,   ih_cov = sir_cov$covariates,   eh_cov = sir_cov$covariates,   init_probs = c(1 - 2 * 1e-10, 1e-10, 1e-10),   iter = 1000,   cores = 4 ) # The output from the model in the previous code chunk is available in the # sir_cov_res package data object  # Get summary statistics, note that non-coefficients parameters are returned on # the logit scale and coefficients are returned on the log scale draws_sum <- summarise_draws(sir_cov_res, "mean", "median",                               ~ quantile2(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) |>   mutate(var_type = c(rep("Infection probability", 2), "Recovery rate", rep("Coefficient", 4))) %>%   mutate(across(where(is.numeric),                 ~ if_else(var_type != "Coefficient",                            plogis(.x),                            exp(.x))))  # "True" values from underlying simulation draws_sum$true_vals <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.2, exp(-0.4), exp(0.7), exp(0.8), exp(0.1))  draws_sum ## # A tibble: 7 × 7 ##   variable    mean  median    q2.5  q97.5 var_type              true_vals ##   <chr>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>                     <dbl> ## 1 eh_prob  0.00957 0.00956 0.00857 0.0107 Infection probability     0.01  ## 2 ih_prob  0.0513  0.0513  0.0435  0.0603 Infection probability     0.05  ## 3 gamma    0.197   0.197   0.187   0.207  Recovery rate             0.2   ## 4 x1_eh    0.631   0.633   0.538   0.744  Coefficient               0.670 ## 5 x2_eh    2.03    2.03    1.75    2.36   Coefficient               2.01  ## 6 x1_ih    2.18    2.18    1.75    2.69   Coefficient               2.23  ## 7 x2_ih    0.844   0.845   0.657   1.08   Coefficient               1.11

title: Multiple Infection Compartments
text: infection process model, infected individuals split two compartments, symptomatic infections () asymptomatic infections (Ia). proportion goes symptomatic compartment governed parameter split. Note although two infectious compartments need provide one value split model enforces proportion going second infectious compartment 1-split. providing parameter name argument (split = "phi") indicating want model fit parameter. also provide numeric value model use directly. also use mult_inf_probs = TRUE argument indicate like two infectious compartments separate (rather single shared) intra-household infection probability.
code: inf_process <- make_infection_model(   transmit(from = "S",            to = c("Is", "Ia"),            source = c("Is", "Ia"),            split = "phi"),   progress(from = "Is", to = "R", gamma_s = NA),   progress(from = "Ia", to = "R", gamma_a = NA),   mult_inf_probs = TRUE)

title: Multiple Infection Compartments
text: observation model composed series named vectors. vector corresponds observation type. entry vector named corresponding compartment infection process model. value probability observing positive observation given individual compartment. example three observation types, first likely positive person actively infectious (e.g. PCR test results), second likely positive person recovered immune infection (e.g. IgG antibody), third indicator whether someone experiencing symptoms. Now ready run model! Now let’s look model results using posterior package.
code: obs_process <- make_observation_model(   pcr = c("S" = 0.05, "Is" = 0.95, "Ia" = 0.95, "R" = 0.05),   igg = c("S" = 0.01, "Is" = 0.01, "Ia" = 0.01, "R" = 0.8),   symp = c("S" = 0.03, "Is" = 1-1e-10, "Ia" = 0.03, "R" = 0.03)) ## Inputs # 1. Infection process model # 2. Observation process model # 3. Raw data # 4. Covariates (optional) # 5. Starting state probabilities  siir_res <- run_model(inf_model = inf_process,                        obs_model = obs_process,                       data = siir,                        init_probs = c(1-3*1e-10, 1e-10, 1e-10, 1e-10),                       iter = 1000,                        cores = 4) # The output from the model in the previous code chunk is available in the # siir_res package data object  # Get summary statistics, note that parameters are returned on the logit scale # so we also transform back to arithmetic scale draws_sum <- summarise_draws(siir_res, "mean", "median",                              ~ quantile2(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) |>   mutate(var_type = c(rep("Infection probability", 3),                       rep("Recovery rate", 2),                       "Symptomatic proportion")) %>%   mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ plogis(.x)))  # "True" values from underlying simulation draws_sum$true_value <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.025, 0.2, 1/3, 0.7)   draws_sum ## # A tibble: 6 × 7 ##   variable      mean  median    q2.5   q97.5 var_type               true_value ##   <chr>        <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>                       <dbl> ## 1 eh_prob    0.00927 0.00928 0.00860 0.00993 Infection probability       0.01  ## 2 ih_prob_Is 0.0440  0.0441  0.0379  0.0510  Infection probability       0.05  ## 3 ih_prob_Ia 0.0225  0.0233  0.0125  0.0362  Infection probability       0.025 ## 4 gamma_s    0.193   0.193   0.180   0.205   Recovery rate               0.2   ## 5 gamma_a    0.321   0.321   0.290   0.352   Recovery rate               0.333 ## 6 phi        0.703   0.703   0.674   0.730   Symptomatic proportion      0.7

title: Create Transmission Probability Matrix — get_transmission_details
text: list following entries: "states", character vector state names "trans_matrix", matrix transition rate values origin (column) destination (row) compartments given. values provided transition rates entry equal 1e-10. "mult_matrix", matrix split values transition origin (column) destination (row) compartments given. split values provided transition rates entry equal 1. "trans_to_fit", data frame information transitions within model, parameter indexing details transition rate fit "mult_to_fit", data frame information splits specified model, parameter indexing details split fit "inf_states", numeric values corresponding indices "states" infectious states "mult_inf_probs", indicator whether infectious states shared separate inta-household infection probabilities. FALSE infection probabilities shared across infectious compartments.

title: Create Transmission Probability Matrix — get_transmission_details
code: # Split the infectious compartment into symptomatic (I_s) and asymptomatic # (I_a) infections, with separate intra-household infection probabilities. inf_model <- make_infection_model(   transmit(from = "S",            to = c("I_s", "I_a"),            source = c("I_s", "I_a"),            split = "phi"),   progress(from = "I_s", to = "R", gamma_s = NA),   progress(from = "I_a", to = "R", gamma_a = NA),   mult_inf_probs = TRUE)  get_transmission_details(inf_model) #> $states #> [1] "S"   "I_s" "I_a" "R"   #>  #> $trans_matrix #>        from_S from_I_s from_I_a from_R #> to_S    1e-10    1e-10    1e-10  1e-10 #> to_I_s  1e-10    1e-10    1e-10  1e-10 #> to_I_a  1e-10    1e-10    1e-10  1e-10 #> to_R    1e-10    1e-10    1e-10  1e-10 #>  #> $mult_matrix #>        from_S from_I_s from_I_a from_R #> to_S        1        1        1      1 #> to_I_s      1        1        1      1 #> to_I_a      1        1        1      1 #> to_R        1        1        1      1 #>  #> $trans_to_fit #>   from  to trans_row trans_col rate_name param source #> 1    S I_s         2         1      <NA>     0   2, 3 #> 2    S I_a         3         1      <NA>     0   2, 3 #> 3  I_s   R         4         2   gamma_s     1      0 #> 4  I_a   R         4         3   gamma_a     2      0 #>  #> $mult_to_fit #>   from  to mult_row mult_col mult_name param #> 1    S I_s        2        1       phi     1 #> 2    S I_a        3        1     1-phi    -1 #>  #> $inf_states #> [1] 2 3 #>  #> $mult_inf_probs #> [1] TRUE #>

code: # Transition from compartment A to B which occurs at rate gamma where # gamma is a user-specified value of 0.2 progress(from = "A", to = "B", gamma = 0.2) #>   from to rate_name rate_value split_name split_value #> 1    A  B     gamma        0.2         NA          NA  # Transition from compartment A to B which occurs at rate gamma where # gamma is fit progress(from = "A", to = "B", gamma = NA) #>   from to rate_name rate_value split_name split_value #> 1    A  B     gamma         NA         NA          NA  # Transition from compartment A split into two destination compartments, B1 # and B2, were individuals leave A at rate delta (fit) and phi (fit) is the # proportion of those who leave A who go into B1 (i.e. 1-phi go into B2). # gamma is fit progress(from = "A", to = c("B1", "B2"), split = "phi", delta = NA) #>   from to rate_name rate_value split_name split_value #> 1    A B1     delta         NA        phi          NA #> 2    A B2     delta         NA      1-phi          NA
